title: China’s Visibility Gap Around the Trump-Xi Summit
gist: China confirmed Xi's Sept 23-25 US visit only two days in advance, and ordinary users on Weibo, WeChat and Xiaohongshu showed little awareness until official media coverage flooded in once the trip began. The piece asks how much ordinary Chinese knew about the summit before state coverage took over.

themes.theme: Information control in Chinese domestic media

insights.claim: Beijing confirmed Xi Jinping's September 23-25, 2026 US visit only on September 21, two days before the trip began.
insights.speaker: Lina Ma
insights.so_what: Late confirmation reflects tight control of summit narrative and limits room for domestic expectations to build.

insights.claim: Before Xi's visit began, visible discussion of the summit among ordinary users on Weibo, WeChat and Xiaohongshu was scarce, and many Chinese people the author spoke with had barely registered the news.
insights.speaker: Lina Ma
insights.so_what: Chinese public sentiment on US relations is largely shaped top-down, so official framing is the signal to watch.
insights.quote: visible discussion among ordinary users on platforms such as Weibo, WeChat, and Xiaohongshu (RedNote) remained scarce

insights.claim: Once the visit was underway, Chinese social media content about the summit was dominated by official outlets emphasizing diplomatic choreography, Trump's reception of Xi and calls for 'constructive strategic stability'.
insights.speaker: Lina Ma
insights.so_what: 'Constructive strategic stability' is Beijing's chosen frame for the relationship and a marker of its desired tone.
